newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid tight supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid tight supply.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. held steady against Tuesday's levels amid tight avaibility of power supply in the region, market sources said.
"Everything is trading sideways. There's not a lot of power running around right now," a Houston trader said.
Despite moderate power demand, limited spot supply from Canada and the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect district have helped support prices in the Northeast, said industry sources.
High fuel costs due to unseasonably strong prices in the domestic natural gas and residual fuel oil markets have kept oil- and gas-fired generating plants off line, they said.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday delivered to Northeast Utilities' territory border was assessed at $33.00-$35.00 a megawatt hour, flat from Tuesday's range for Wednesday's delivery.
Non-firm, next-day NEPOOL power during light demand hours at the NU border was again quoted at $21.00-$22.00.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm electricity in the eastern portion of the grid for Thursday was pegged at $29.50-$30.00, a tighter range than Tuesday's $29.00-$30.00.
Off-peak, non-firm NYPP power into eastern NYPP for next-day delivery was quoted again near $17.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices were discussed near $19.50, compared with a quote of $19.00-$20.00 on Tuesday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for delivery into western NYPP was still valued near $14.00.
